label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Tolu, I'm inside it right now. Biology 100L, federal uni here in Lagos. I wrote JAMB 2025, scored 251, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and they gave me Biology. So your post is literally me last year.

The day I saw Biology on the portal, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat that day. My mum was still telling people in church that I'm doing medicine for like two months after, and I had to beg her to stop. So the crying since afternoon, I understand it. You're not overreacting.

Now the transfer, because that's the main thing you asked.

It is real. Kingsley saying it's a myth is not true. But favour saying "just read hard" is too simple. This is what our level adviser told us, and note that it's for my own school:

1. You need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 after 100L.
2. There must be space in Medicine. If there's no space, your 4.5 will not help you.
3. You must have met the Medicine cut-offs in both JAMB and post-UTME in the first place.

She also said that last year about 6 people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 applied. That's the whole faculty o, not Biology alone.

On number 3, I can't tell you whether your 268 is enough. I don't know your school's Medicine cut-off and I don't know what you scored in post-UTME. Check both of them. 268 alone doesn't tell anybody whether you qualify, so I don't know how Kingsley can say "you're almost there".

And so you know where I'm talking from, my CGPA after first semester is 4.31. That's not 4.5. I'm still trying, but I've not transferred and I can't promise you I will.

So please don't accept Biology with the mind that transfer is automatic. Your dad is right that it's possible. Your aunty is also not totally wrong, because most people that enter Biology do finish in Biology. If you accept, accept knowing you may do the full four years there.

Now, how it really is inside. In 100L you're doing BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Biology and chemistry you can manage. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people. If you're chasing 4.5, those two are where the wahala is.

Money too, so it doesn't surprise you. My lab coat was 6,500, the dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual is extra on top.

You also asked if Biology is bad as a course or it's just that your mind was on Medicine. For me it was my mind. In our first BIO practical we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and I was fine. That was the day I realised I actually like this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. Biology is not a bad course. It's just not the one we filled in the form.

About rewriting. People say "one year is nothing", but staying at home is not as easy as they make it sound. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer so she could rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times since then and she's still at home. I'm not saying that will be you. I'm saying nobody can guarantee you Medicine next year, the same way nobody can guarantee you transfer. But rewriting is not wrong either, if you're really ready for it and you know what the year will look like.

What I'd do if I were you:

- Before that acceptance fee deadline, go to the faculty or the department in your own school and ask for their exact transfer rules: the CGPA, the cut-offs, and how many people they actually moved last year. Don't just trust forum people, including me. Every school has its own rules, and what my adviser told me may not be what yours will tell you.
- Check your post-UTME score and the Medicine cut-off for this year, so you know how far you really were.
- Ask yourself, when nobody is around, whether you want Medicine itself or you just want to be "doctor" for your parents. I had to ask myself that too, and my answer was not as straightforward as I thought it would be. Your answer matters, because either way you'll be working hard for one more year, whether in Biology or at home, and you should know what you're working for.

If you want Medicine and nothing else, and you can handle one more year at home, then rewrite with your full chest. If you can see yourself living with Biology even if the transfer doesn't work out, then accept it and give 100L everything.

Whichever one you choose, it's not the end of the world, I promise you. Last year I thought my life had scattered. This year I'm in the lab cutting toads and arguing about genetics. You'll be fine, Tolu.

If you want to ask me anything about 100L, just reply here. I'll answer.
